_comment: Recipes of the stage-2 sound studio (room 27) and props (room 32) area (prefix soundprops).

Movie records: 10 x 0x344 bytes at 0x455aa1, count 0x457b49. +0x148 minutes, +0x14c state (3 = shot), +0x184 cutting state (3 = cut), +0x198 sound state (0 none, 1 being added, 3 done), +0x19c sound track (0x13..0x1c, the sound id chosen in DDF 70), +0x1a0/+0x1a4/+0x1a8 day, month, year the sound track was started, +0x1ac sound days ((minutes / 10) >> 2, at least 1).
Sound equipment: 10 slots of 16 bytes at 0x458379 (+0 EQUIP.TAP index, +4 condition, +8 value, +0xc -1), count 0x458419.

soundprops_base.note: prod_s2staff (all production buildings rented, one employee per job: dubber 418 and sound engineer 447 working, both level 6; cutter 193 level 6; copying girl 257 and warehousewoman 286 working; account 1500000, 8:00 on 1-1-1997, WET plot, 'ProdAll' at 300,119) plus one shot and cut movie without sound and one copying machine, patched: movie count 0x457b49 = 1, record 0 'Sound Test', 80 minutes (+0x148), state 3 (+0x14c), cut (+0x184 = 3), no sound (+0x198 = 0), quality values +0x2f8/+0x2fc/+0x300/+0x30c = 60; copier slot 0 (0x459289) = (29 'Emil Copy 5000', condition 100, value 2, -1), count 0x459329 = 1 (what the game writes when it buys that machine, see cutcopy_copier), so the office laptop can put the movie on sale. Slow clock (0x4556bc = 30, 31 timer calls per game minute) so that no hourly event interrupts the scripts.

soundprops_mixing.note: soundprops_base after the game bought sound equipment and started the sound track of the movie (script soundprops_mixing.txt): in room 27 'Buy equipment' -> '3 Mix 3000' (1200 $) -> Buy; 'Add sound track to film' (DDF 60, callback 0x42de52) -> 'Sound Test' -> DDF 70 (callback 0x42e0c4) -> 'Tango' -> Listen -> thumb -> 'Adding sound track will take about 2 day(s).'; saved on the WET plot as 'Mixing' in slot 4 (Load-dialog entry 300,119). Clock patched back to 8:00 and the minute countdown 0x4556c0 to 0. The game wrote: account 1500000 - 1200 = 1498800; sound slot 0 = (45 '3 Mix 3000', condition 100, value 3, -1), count 0x458419 = 1; movie 0 sound state +0x198 = 1, track +0x19c = 0x19 ('Tango' is control 8 of DDF 70, track = control + 0x11), start date +0x1a0/+0x1a4/+0x1a8 = 1-1-1997, sound days +0x1ac = (80 / 10) >> 2 = 2.

soundprops_d3clock.note: Patch-only parent of soundprops_day3: soundprops_mixing with the clock set to Wednesday 3-1-1997 9:59 (day 0x45569c = 3, weekday 0x4556b8 = 2) and the normal speed (0x4556bc = 3).

soundprops_day3.note: soundprops_d3clock loaded and run past 10:00, saved as 'SndDay3' on the WET plot (Load-dialog entry 300,119). At 10:00 the hourly dispatcher calls 0x42ddff, which compares the days since the sound track was started (0x405314 on +0x1a0: 3 - 1 = 2) with the sound days (+0x1ac = 2) using '>', so the sound track is still being added (+0x198 = 1). Then patched to the slow clock (0x4556bc = 30) and 10:00.

soundprops_d4clock.note: Patch-only parent of soundprops_sounddone: soundprops_mixing with the clock set to Thursday 4-1-1997 9:59 (day 0x45569c = 4, weekday 0x4556b8 = 3) and the normal speed (0x4556bc = 3).

soundprops_sounddone.note: soundprops_d4clock loaded and run past 10:00, saved as 'SndDone' on the WET plot (Load-dialog entry 300,119). At 10:00 0x42ddff finds 4 - 1 = 3 days > +0x1ac = 2 and sets the sound state +0x198 = 3 (done). Then patched to the slow clock (0x4556bc = 30) and 10:00, so later scripts are not interrupted by hourly events.

soundprops_props.note: prod_s2staff (all production buildings rented, one employee per job: set builder 280 level 6, props assistant 394 level 6 and props manageress 550 level 9 working; account 1500000, 8:00 on 1-1-1997, WET plot, 'ProdAll' at 300,119) with a slow clock (0x4556bc = 30, 31 timer calls per game minute), so that no hourly event (10:00 marketing roll 0x42f334, 13:00 sabotage roll 0x43070e) calls rand() or shows a box during the props scripts. The props room setup 0x42c28f rolls rand() % 100 > 90 on every entry; with the runner's fixed clock and no clock-driven rand() calls the third entry after loading this save is the one that starts the talk (strings 1406-1414).

soundprops_list.note: soundprops_base with one '3 Mix 3000' in the sound studio (slot 0x458379 = (45, 100, 3, -1), what the game writes in soundprops_mixing; count 0x458419 = 1) and five more movie records (count 0x457b49 = 6), to test the filter of the DDF 60 list in 0x42de52 (movie i is listed in control 13 + i only when state +0x14c = 3, sound state +0x198 = 0 and cutting state +0x184 = 3): 1 'Not Cut' (state 3, cut 0), 2 'Being Cut' (state 3, cut 1), 3 'Has Sound' (state 3, cut 3, sound 3), 4 'Still Planned' (state 1, cut 3), 5 'Short Film' (20 minutes, state 3, cut 3, sound 0: (20 / 10) >> 2 = 0, raised to 1 day). Name and Load-dialog entry stay 'ProdAll' (300,119).

soundprops_propsets.note: soundprops_props after the game bought two sets and sold one in the props room (script soundprops_propsets.txt): 'Buy sets' -> 'Castle Everrandy' (21000 $) -> Buy -> 'City Sex' (12000 $) -> Buy -> sell list 'City Sex' (10800 $ = 12000 * 90 / 100) -> Sell; saved on the WET plot as 'PropSets' in slot 4 (Load-dialog entry 300,119). Clock patched back to 8:00 and the minute countdown 0x4556c0 to 0. The purchase writes slot 0 = (42 'Castle Everrandy', condition 100, value 5, -1) and slot 1 = (City Sex); the sale clears slot 1 back to -1 and the count 0x459285 is the number of used slots (1).
